question: What organ performs oxygen exchange for the growing foetus?
explanation: Because the lungs are not yet breathing air, the placenta takes over the job of bringing in oxygen and removing waste. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h1)

question: Why does the foetal circulatory system bypass the lungs?

options.A: The heart pumps too slowly to reach the chest
options.B: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not oxygenate blood yet
options.C: The lungs are too small to receive blood flow
options.D: Oxygen is only needed in the lower body

explanation: Foetal lungs are collapsed and non-functional for breathing, so blood is shunted away from them toward the placenta. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h1)

question: What is the primary job of the umbilical vein?

options.A: Drain deoxygenated blood from the lower limbs
options.B: Carry waste products away from the baby's heart
options.C: Carry oxygen-rich blood from the placenta to the foetus
options.D: Supply blood directly to the foetal lungs

explanation: The umbilical vein brings fresh, oxygenated blood straight from the mother's placenta into the baby's body. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h2)

question: Where does the ductus venosus send most of its blood?
explanation: The ductus venosus acts as a shortcut, routing umbilical blood past the liver to empty right into the inferior vena cava. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h2)

question: What is the foramen ovale?

options.A: A valve inside the umbilical cord
options.B: An opening between the right and left atria
options.C: A vessel connecting the liver to the heart
options.D: An artery carrying blood to the placenta

explanation: The foramen ovale is a hole in the heart wall separating the upper chambers, letting blood cross straight over. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the ductus arteriosus in a foetus?

options.A: To direct blood from the pulmonary artery into the aorta
options.B: To send deoxygenated blood back to the placenta
options.C: To bypass the liver and feed the brain
options.D: To close the gap between the heart ventricles

explanation: The ductus arteriosus catches blood heading toward the lungs and reroutes it into the aorta to feed the body. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h3)

question: Which part of the foetal body receives the highest concentration of freshly oxygenated blood?
explanation: The foramen ovale directs the freshest, most oxygen-rich blood toward the upper body to support the rapidly growing brain and heart. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h4)

question: A newborn has a persistent shunt directing blood from the pulmonary artery to the aorta. What structure failed to manage this normal foetal pathway?
explanation: The ductus arteriosus is the specific vessel connecting the pulmonary artery to the aorta during foetal life. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h4)

question: What makes foetal hemoglobin different from adult hemoglobin?

options.A: It is produced exclusively in the placenta
options.B: It has a higher affinity for oxygen
options.C: It carries carbon dioxide instead of oxygen
options.D: It breaks down much faster in cold temperatures

explanation: Foetal hemoglobin grabs onto oxygen much more tightly, enabling the baby to extract oxygen from maternal blood. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h5)

question: Why is pulmonary vascular resistance high in the un-born foetus?

options.A: The liver blocks blood flow to the chest
options.B: The heart pumps with too much force
options.C: The umbilical cord constricts the chest
options.D: The lungs are collapsed and filled with fluid

explanation: Unexpanded, fluid-filled lungs squeeze the small blood vessels tightly, causing high resistance that keeps blood away from them. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h5)

question: What triggers the immediate closing of the foramen ovale at birth?

options.A: Increased blood pressure in the left side of the heart
options.B: The complete digestion of foetal hemoglobin
options.C: The physical clamping of the umbilical cord by the doctor
options.D: A sudden drop in the baby's body temperature

explanation: When the lungs open up and blood flows back into the left atrium, the pressure rises and pushes the flap of the foramen ovale closed. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h6)

question: A newborn baby experiences a sudden drop in blood oxygen levels shortly after delivery. Which foetal shunt is most likely to remain open or reopen due to this stress?
explanation: Low oxygen levels and respiratory distress in a newborn can keep the muscular ductus arteriosus open or cause it to dilate. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h6)
